claims.text: Combining ab initio free-energy calculations with CALPHAD will accurately and efficiently predict melting and liquid-phase thermodynamic properties across the high-entropy-alloy family.
EMTO-CPA/DFT methods can incorporate finite-temperature electronic, magnetic, and phononic free-energy contributions.
The relevant initial state is a high-temperature disordered, paramagnetic solid solution.
Configurational entropy dominates in the high-temperature solid-solution state.
CALPHAD efficiently determines multicomponent phase diagrams from Gibbs free energies and diffusion mobilities.
CALPHAD supplies phase-stability and composition-temperature information for complex multicomponent alloys.
DFT/EMTO-CPA captures the local electronic structure relevant to alloy thermodynamics.
Electronic, magnetic, and phononic contributions are significant near the melting point.
The approach applies when alloys are in a nearly random solid-solution state.
CALPHAD provides a database-driven treatment of complex phase equilibria and liquid-phase behavior.
Combining ab initio calculations and CALPHAD mitigates limitations of either method used alone.
The integrated method extends predictive capability to melting and liquid-phase thermodynamic properties.
Predicted melting temperature, fusion enthalpy, fusion entropy, and melting volume change will be within approximately 5–10% of experiment.
The integrated approach will provide a reliable proxy for experiments across the high-entropy-alloy family.
Pure ab initio or pure CALPHAD approaches typically have larger errors for liquid properties and phase transitions.
Significant short-range order or clustering below the near-melting regime may increase prediction uncertainty.
Prediction quality depends on CALPHAD database coverage and approximations in DFT and CPA.
Deviation greater than approximately 10% across multiple alloys, or failure to reproduce liquid-thermodynamic trends, would falsify the hypothesis.
